frames.narration: Job: count page views per URL. The input is split into 2 blocks of 1,000 views each, one per mapper. There are 2 reducers.
Map: each mapper reads its block next to the data and emits one (url, 1) record per view. 1,000 records each, 2,000 in total.
Combiner: each mapper pre-sums its own output before it leaves the machine. 1,000 records collapse to 40, one per distinct URL, so only 80 cross the network.
Partition: each record is assigned to reducer hash(url) mod 2 and written to the mapper's local disk, sorted by key. Same URL, same reducer, always.
Shuffle: each reducer pulls its partition from every mapper over the network. This all-to-all copy is the expensive step. Reducer 1 receives 38 records, Reducer 2 receives 42.
Merge and reduce: each reducer merges the sorted runs from both mappers, so equal URLs sit together, then sums each group and writes its output file.

Skew: /home is 60% of all views. Without the combiner, all 1,200 of its records would go to one reducer, which would then hold 1,200 of the 2,000 records while the other waits. The job ends when the slowest reducer ends.

A combiner cut /home to 2 records here. For joins or medians there is nothing to pre-sum, so the fix is salting: spread /home over keys like /home#0 and /home#1, then merge the partial counts in a small second stage.
